issues.description: The constructor parameter order in the solution for ExcellenceLand does not follow the ordering required by the problem statement/UML. The problem/UML lists attributes (excellencyLevel: double, excellentEnough: boolean) and (by task text) the rides attribute of type List<Ride>. The exercise instructs that constructors must accept attributes in the same order as in the UML (and for subclasses the superclass attributes first). The solution's constructor is declared as ExcellenceLand(List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel) which places rides first and reverses the order of excellencyLevel and excellentEnough. This contradicts the explicit constructor-order requirement and will confuse or break student implementations and automated checks that expect the UML-specified order.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the ExcellenceLand constructor parameters follow the attribute order as specified by the UML/problem statement. For example, declare the constructor as: public ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) and assign the parameters to the corresponding fields in that same order. Alternatively, clarify in the problem statement the intended order for the association attribute 'rides' (e.g., list it after the other attributes) so the expected constructor signature is unambiguous.
